content.text: {"route":"gap","reason":"The record has material gaps that should be filled before a merits decision. The agency's own Preliminary Fact-Finding Report found that S1 falsely accused Complainant of assault and that staff feared S1's retribution, yet the final decision does not address it. A Nurse Manager said the light-duty comparator was treated differently without explanation and called the reassignment suspicious and unjustified, and the decision's pretext analysis does not engage with that. The record shows no testimony from S1 or the comparator, no age or disability comparator analysis, and no inquiry into whether the MSA position conflicted with the medical restrictions. The Employee Health release slip bearing on the AWOL charge is not examined. Claim 4 (the medical retirement remark) is never analyzed. The reprisal finding rests on a narrow view of protected activity, with no look at earlier EEO activity or at harassment as a whole. Claim 1 was dismissed, though it is part of the harassment pattern."}
